blocks.text: Antiviral and antiretroviral drugs act against viruses rather than bacteria. Antiretroviral drugs are one particular group of antivirals.

blocks.alt: A large blue oval labelled antiviral drugs, for hepatitis, influenza and herpes viruses, contains a smaller red oval labelled antiretroviral drugs, which treat retroviruses such as HIV. A note says retroviruses have an RNA genome and use reverse transcriptase, and that all antiretrovirals are antivirals but not all antivirals are antiretrovirals.
blocks.caption: Antiretrovirals are a subset of antivirals (original diagram for this topic).
blocks.long_description: Antiviral drugs treat viral infections by preventing viruses from growing and multiplying in the body; they act against viruses such as those of hepatitis, influenza and herpes. Antiretroviral drugs are a special group of antivirals for retroviruses such as HIV, viruses with RNA as their genetic material that replicate using the enzyme reverse transcriptase; they help the immune system and stop HIV from multiplying. So every antiretroviral is an antiviral, but not every antiviral is an antiretroviral.

blocks.explanation: No. All antiretrovirals are antivirals, but antivirals also include drugs for non-retroviruses such as influenza and herpes viruses.

items: Antivirals act on viruses; antiretrovirals are the antivirals for retroviruses.
